question: Should OpenClaw support descriptive client attribution, cryptographically verifiable egress identity, or no universal agent-origin claim—and which outbound paths must that guarantee cover?
rationale: These choices have materially different security meaning, privacy impact, key ownership, enforceability, and core-versus-plugin architecture, so repository inspection cannot safely choose the policy.

options.title: Design verified egress identity
options.body: Specify a protected signing authority, audience and replay rules, key lifecycle, privacy limits, and enforceable outbound-path coverage before adding a generic integration seam.

options.title: Add attribution only
options.body: Permit opt-in domain-scoped headers while documenting that they identify an OpenClaw client configuration and do not prove autonomous-agent origin.

options.title: Keep trust service-specific
options.body: Use API credentials, OAuth, mTLS, gateways, or plugin-owned handshakes instead of defining a universal OpenClaw attestation claim.

recommendation.title: Design verified egress identity
recommendation.body: Specify a protected signing authority, audience and replay rules, key lifecycle, privacy limits, and enforceable outbound-path coverage before adding a generic integration seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing product/security review and adjacent attribution history provide the strongest available decision-routing signal.
